what: One real sponsored send on chipnet (Bitcoin Cash's public test network). Built and checked by the same functions the app uses: buildSponsoredSend (src/core/sponsoredSend.ts) builds it, toWizardRequest (src/core/wizard.ts) makes the sign request, src/core/headlessSigner.ts signs input 0 only (sighash 0x61) in place of a wallet, and verifySignedTx (src/core/wizard.ts) checks it on the BCH 2026 VM before broadcast. Built, signed and broadcast by `npx tsx scripts/chipnet-spike.ts --network chipnet`; the 'readback' field below records the chain read-back and explorer check done after that run (not script output).
not: Not mainnet and not PUSD: PUSD exists only on mainnet, so the genesis tx mints a test fungible token that stands in for it (same covenant rules, constructor category = the test token). The user key is a headless test key, not a named wallet.
genesis: mints the test token, seeds one pool lane with 100,000 sats + 1 unit (R7), gives the user key one 1,000-sat coin holding 200 units and no other BCH

inputs: in0: user coin, 1,000 sats + 200 units, signed by the user key
in1: pool lane, 100,000 sats + 1 unit, unlocked by the covenant (no key)
outputs: out0: 651 sats + 10 units to the recipient
out1: 651 sats + 189 units change to the user
out2: 99,118 sats + 2 units back to the pool (1 seed + exactly 1 fee unit, R5)
sponsoredSend.laneSubsidyNote: 580 miner fee + 302 sats top-up: the user coin held 1,000 sats and the two token outputs need 651 each (R6 allows at most 675)

readback: both txids fetched back from a chipnet Fulcrum server with ElectrumNetworkProvider('chipnet') on 2026-11-20 after broadcast; outputs above are from that readback; the explorer above showed it with 5 confirmations at 572 B, fee 580 sats, on 2026-11-20 20:40 UTC
